authorization.scope_quoted: round-8 instruction (delivered directly by the user): R8-P1-HAR-REPLICATION only; reuse the existing HAR data / TIDES / torch / checkpoint contract; exactly two new trainings with seeds 101 and 102 (or the first two unused integers >= 101); research cap wall 1800 s, process CPU 3600 s, threads <= 2, RAM <= 16 GiB; installation and PDF builds under the separate common limit; no new data, model, architecture, hyper-parameter or extra diagnostic sweep
authorization.not_approved: a third seed, any change of split/normalization/network/optimizer/update count/checkpoint rule, a per-token or cancellation diagnostic, pooling of runs into one sample

question: How sensitive are the P1-HAR-01 decomposition and risk results (primary H8 CE(mean) - CE(time); C0/S8/H8 secondaries; the S8 common-endpoint pooled decomposition) to the model initialization and minibatch order, with the data, subjects, splits, normalization and protocol held fixed?
not_a_replication_of: an independent dataset (the training data and the 9 test subjects are reused) or a general training-run effect (two extra seeds of one architecture)
preserved_verdicts: PRIMARY_HAR_RISK_DIFFERENCE_NOT_ESTABLISHED (the original P1-HAR-01 primary is not retro-updated or pooled with the new runs)

seeds.used_before_in_this_project: HAR model seed 0 (P1-HAR-01); synthetic model seeds 0-4 (P1-REAL-01/02); toy unit seeds 0-31 and 999 (FIRST_RUN); 101 and 102 were never used, so they are used as requested
seeds.rng_separation: seed s is set in python random, numpy's global RNG (TIDES initialization draws from it) and torch immediately before model construction (model RNG); the minibatch sampler is a separate random.Random(s) instance (order RNG); the data, splits and normalization statistics are fixed arrays from P1-HAR-01 and involve no RNG; the subject bootstrap uses random.Random(0) through scssm.real.stats.draws, as in P1-HAR-01
seeds.test_subjects: the SAME 9 official test subjects (2947 windows) as P1-HAR-01 are reused; this is stated wherever the results are reported

inputs_and_hashes.runner: scripts/run_p1_har_r8.py (a minimal extension that imports the P1-HAR-01 helpers unchanged: grid, native_batch, locf_resample, build, setup, load_cache, train_loop, eval_mode_checks)
inputs_and_hashes.model_and_protocol: identical to configs/p1_har_01.json: TIDESClassifier with the pilot backbone kwargs (23,786 parameters), 9 channels, 6 classes; Adam lr 0.003, batch 32, 2000 updates; calibration subjects 7, 15, 17, 19 every 100 updates, lowest calibration cross-entropy kept (earliest on ties); fit-only normalization; 128 held intervals of 1/50 s; eval mode, float32, 2 threads

arms.native_mean: official readout (head of the token-mean features)
arms.native_time: head of the dt_j/T-weighted features (inference ablation)
arms.resampled: LOCF onto the training grid; its input equals the C0 input exactly on S8 and H8 (checked; P1-HAR-01 showed bit-identical logits for identical input), so its logits are the C0 logits and no separate forward is spent

evaluation_per_checkpoint.one_forward_per_condition: C0, S8 and H8 are each run once in batches of 256 windows; the common-end-point outputs (S8 end tokens 8k) and the H8 per-token logits are taken from the same forward passes and stored in float64 pooled form; no forward is repeated and no timing block is run (cost was measured in P1-HAR-01)
evaluation_per_checkpoint.primary: d_s = mean over windows of subject s of [CE(native_mean, H8) - CE(native_time, H8)]; D = equal-weight mean over the 9 subjects; subject-level paired percentile bootstrap (2000 draws, seed 0) per run
evaluation_per_checkpoint.secondary: per arm and condition: CE, accuracy, prediction flips vs C0, total variation vs C0, class-centered relative logit distance vs C0 (exclusion rule ||ztilde_C0|| < 1e-6 as before); H8 logit decomposition W, M, M_end, Q (norms, subject-first); S8 common-end-point decomposition z_all - z0 = (z_end - z0) + (z_all - z_end) with class-centered relative norms (per-window ratios, subject-first), inner product, and CE/flip of z_end (the same definitions as P1-HAR-CT-01)
evaluation_per_checkpoint.analysis_unit: subject (9 clusters); subject means first, then equal weight; the three runs (original seed 0, seeds 101 and 102) are reported as separate rows and never pooled into 27 observations; no pooled p-value

solver_precision: float32 forward in torch.inference_mode(); pooled logits stored as float64; no float64 forward

stop_conditions.immediate_stop: leakage (test subjects used in any training decision), a split mismatch with data_hash.json, a config hash mismatch, a non-finite loss or non-finite logit (the estimand is undefined), a label/evaluator change, resource exceedance
stop_conditions.not_a_stop: a null, mixed or unfavourable result, an interval including 0, a sign that differs from the original run
stop_conditions.engineering_bug: one minimal fix that does not change the contract plus one re-run of the affected stage; the original attempt is kept as INVALID with its scope

budget.projection_from_P1_HAR_01: train 183 s wall / 354 s CPU per seed; eval without the timing block about 90 s wall / 170 s CPU per seed; two seeds about 550 s wall / 1050 s CPU
budget.ledger: results/raw/R8-P1-HAR-REPLICATION/cost_ledger.json; the timer starts before importing torch; wall and process CPU separately; a stage refuses to start if the ledger plus its projection would exceed a cap; no duplicate process of the same run is started (a lock file per stage)

skip_rule: a stage whose outputs exist with the recorded config/runner/data hashes and a COMPLETED status is skipped and its evidence hash is listed under completed_stages
next_command: none: the finite stage list is complete; no further stage is queued
